card.statement:
Let $X = k[x_1, x_2]/I$, where $I = (x_1^p, x_2^p)$ if $char(k) = p >0$ and $I = 0$ if $char(k) = 0$.
Let $L$ be a Lie algebra over a field $k$, $H$ an ideal of $L$ such that

$$L = H  \leftthreetimes L_0, \hbox{ where }L_0 \simeq {\mathcal H}.$$

Let

$$\theta : H \to L$$

be a Lie algebra homomorphism such that :

1. there is $m  \in {\mathbb N}$ such that for every $b \in \{ y_1, y_2 \}$ and $h \in H$ we have $\theta(b^m \circ h) = 0$. If $char(k) = p >0$ we furthermore have that $m = p$.

2. $\theta(y_1 y_3 \circ h) = \theta(y_2 \circ h)$ and $\theta(y_3 \circ h) = 0$ for every $h \in H$.

Then
there is a homomorphism of Lie algebras

$$\psi :  L \to L \wr {\mathcal Der } X = (X \otimes L) \leftthreetimes {\mathcal Der}X
$$

given by

\begin{equation}
\psi(h) =
\sum_{0 \leq i_1, i_2 \leq m_0 = m-1} ( i_1 ! i_2 !)^{-1} x_1^{i_1} x_2^{i_2}  \otimes
\theta(y_1^{i_1} y_2^{i_2} \circ h) \hbox{ for } h \in H,
\end{equation}

where $\theta$ is the virtual endomorphism associated to $\psi$ with respect to the augmentation map $\epsilon : X \to k$ i.e. $\epsilon$ is the $k$-algebra homomorphism defined by $\epsilon(x_i) = 0$ for $1 \leq i \leq 2$ and $\psi(y_i) = \partial / \partial {x_i}$ for $ 1 \leq i \leq 2$ and
$\psi(y_3) = x_1 \partial / \partial x_2$;
card.label: Theorem 6

paper.title: On self-similar Lie algebras and virtual endomorphisms
paper.abstract: We introduce the notion of virtual endomorphisms of Lie algebras and use it as an approach for constructing self-similarity of Lie algebras. This is done in particular for a class of metabelian Lie algebras having homological type F Pn, which are variants of lamp-lighter groups. We establish several criteria when the existence of virtual endomorphism implies a self-similar Lie structure. Furthermore, we prove that the classical Lie algebra sln(k), where char(k) does not divide n affords non-trivial faithful self-similarity.
